neighbor_comparisons.actual_core_read: Read as a spectral-completeness statement for the heat kernel of the PSL_2(Z) Cayley graph: the proposition states an orthonormality/completeness identity for the eigenfunction family, and the proof is a contour-integration and residue computation. It does not state that a return probability has growth rate rho(G), and no Fekete or supermultiplicativity argument appears in it.
neighbor_comparisons.reason_target_distinct: Statement identity and non-identity: the neighbor asserts completeness of an eigenfunction family for one Cayley graph; the target asserts two quantitative facts about P_o[X_n=o] and rho(G) for an arbitrary graph. No specialization either way covers the other.

neighbor_comparisons.actual_counted_statement:
\begin{theorem}[$\Poin(p,p)$]\label{main:tracial}
Let $(\M,\tau)$ be a tracial von Neumann algebra and $(T_t)_{t\ge0}=e^{-tL}$ a $\tau$--symmetric quantum Markov semigroup with fixed-point algebra $\N$ and conditional expectation $E:\M\to\N$.
If $\{T_t\}_{t\ge0}$ has a spectral gap $\alpha>0$, then for every self-adjoint $x$ in the domain of $L$ and $p=2$ or $p\ge3$, it satisfies the Poincar\'e inequality $\Poin(p,p)$ with constant $\tfrac{p}{\sqrt{2\alpha}}$, i.e.,
\[
\|x-E(x)\|_{L^p(\M,\tau)}  \le  \frac{p}{\sqrt{2\alpha}} \|\Gamma(x,x)\|^{1/2}_{L^{p/2}(\M,\tau)}.
\]
\end{theorem}
neighbor_comparisons.actual_core_read: Read as a Poincare(p,p) inequality for tracial quantum Markov semigroups with constant p/sqrt(2 alpha) from a spectral gap alpha > 0, proved by triangle inequalities on the Gamma semi-norm after a finite-dimensional reduction; its first proof line cites its own label (\Cref{main:tracial}). It is an inequality between Dirichlet forms, not a statement about return-probability growth on a graph.
neighbor_comparisons.reason_target_distinct: The neighbor is a Poincare inequality whose constant is stated in terms of a gap; the Fekete argument of the target and its all-n pointwise bound do not follow from such an inequality without substantial additional work, and the neighbor does not claim them.
